geometry.radial_pitch: constant at the mean P/D (the B-series radial pitch distribution is not available offline; it is not invented here)

citation.title: Further computer-analyzed data of the Wageningen B-screw series
citation.content: 39-term KT and 47-term KQ multiple regression of the Wageningen B-screw series open-water tests, valid Z=2-7, Ae/Ao=0.30-1.05, P/D=0.5-1.4, Re=2e6 at the 0.75R chord, hub ratio 0.18-0.20

provenance.declared_limit: the printed NSMB tables are not available offline in this worktree; the coefficients enter through the two-step machine chain below and the regression is additionally adjudicated against physics anchors (tests/test_wageningen_anchor.py) rather than trusted on faith

chain.what: published regression tables of Oosterveld & van Oossanen (1975)

platform reference implementation; its own provenance note records a programmatic extraction from two independent public implementations (AlfredMylne/PropCalc, isulovsky/Wageningen-B-series-propeller-calculator, fetched 2026-11-01, agreeing term for term)
this extraction (importlib read of the coefficient tuples, no retyping)

criteria.statement: every point with J <= 0.8 has |dKT| < 15.0% and |dKQ| < 15.0% (highest-fidelity configuration)
ablation axes quantified and additive: sum(phi) == v(all) - v(none) to 1e-9 relative, with the model-form remainder reported

probe.rule: numerically stable iff |KT| <= 1.0 and |KQ| <= 0.2 (blow-ups are 1e2..1e6; physical points stay inside these bounds even past zero thrust)

kp505.design_advance_note: the design advance of the KP505 anchor module is the argmax of the anchor efficiency column, which is J = 0.8; it coincides with the advance of the historically logged deviation, so 'decomposition_design_J' and 'decomposition_J_0.8' are the same point
